newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Party reformers break with Romania's Iliescu.
newsitem.headline: Party reformers break with Romania's Iliescu.

text.p: Defeated reformers completed their break with Romania's former president Ion Iliescu on Wednesday by announcing the founding of a new leftist party.
"Our party will be called the Alliance for Romania," Teodor Melescanu, a former foreign minister, told reporters. "We don't intend to clone the PDSR, from which we split on moral criteria."
The Party of Social Democracy ruled for Romania's first seven post-communist years until defeated by centrists in November's parliamentary election.

It is now the main opposition party and is still dominated by former communists around Iliescu, who swept to power during the 1989 revolution in which Stalinist ruler Nicolae Ceausescu was overthrown and shot.
The split began at a conference last week when Iliescu blocked calls for sweeping change and rejected the urging of dissidents that he dump associates tainted by corruption scandals.
Iliescu, who was confirmed as PDSR president at last week's conference, dismissed the calls for reform as "elitist".
Melescanu, flanked by Iliescu's former campaign manager Iosif Boda and former reform minister Mircea Cosea, appealed to other party technocrats to join their revolt.
Iliescu had persuaded Melescanu and Cosea to join the PDSR shortly before last year's elections, in a bid to rejuvenate the party.
Melescanu said his Alliance for Romania -- "a centre-left party, patterned on a modern Social Democratic doctrine" -- would be officially registered later on Wednesday.
It would support centrist reforms aimed at boosting local capital markets and would aim to draw support from Romania's emerging private entrepreneurs, he said.
